title: Generation or editing — pick the mode
scenario: A bakery wants their product photo kept exactly as it is — same pastry, same plate — but with the background replaced by a warm café table scene. Everything about the pastry itself must stay identical.
task: Which mode fits the task best?

options.text: Generate a fresh image describing a pastry on a café table
options.feedback: You would be rebuilding the pastry from words — shape, texture and plating will drift. The brief says everything about it must stay identical.

options.text: Edit the existing photo: keep the pastry, describe only the new background
options.feedback: Exactly — an edit changes what you ask for and preserves the rest. One variable changes; the product photo stays trustworthy.

options.text: Generate many fresh images and pick the one that looks most similar
options.feedback: Similar is not identical. For product imagery, a close-enough pastry is simply the wrong pastry.

hints: Ask: is the goal to construct something new, or to change one thing in an image that already exists?
explanation: Generation constructs from your words; editing transforms an image you supply. The moment a brief contains “keep everything else the same”, you want an edit — ideally on a selected region. That single choice is the difference between a product photo and a product photo of something that is no longer your product.
